mainTopic: Women and the קרבן פסח on פסח ראשון and פסח שני, women's obligation in מצה, and the start of the משנה about an אונן eating the פסח.
overview: This amud opens with the last word of the previous discussion, פריצותא. The גמרא then quotes a full ברייתא with three opinions about women and the קרבן פסח: may we slaughter for a woman alone, only let her join a group (טפילה), or not slaughter for her at all, on פסח ראשון and on פסח שני? The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, and רבי שמעון each read the פסוקים, especially 'במכסת נפשות', 'האיש ההוא', and 'ככל חקת הפסח'. It then searches for the exact 'איש' verse רבי שמעון uses and settles on 'מאיש לפי אכלו', which teaches two laws. Next, after fixing its wording, the גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר's ruling about women and the two פסחים follows רבי יהודה. רבי יוחנן teaches that a פסח group should not be made up only of גרים. A ברייתא about פסח, מצה and מרור is reread so that it fits רבי אלעזר's rule that women are obligated to eat מצה by Torah law. Finally, a new משנה rules that an אונן may eat his קרבן פסח at night but not other קדשים, and begins a case that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing word of the previous discussion: the concern of immorality
steps.stepSummary: The single word פריצותא ends the earlier discussion. It gives the reason a certain group (slaves together with minors) should not be formed for the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Because of] immorality.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last word of the previous discussion, not the start of a new one. It gives the reason a certain kind of קרבן פסח group should not be formed: the concern of immoral behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked why some groups (like a group of slaves together with minors) may not be formed for eating the קרבן פסח. The answer is פריצותא, a worry about improper conduct. With this word that topic is closed, and the next line starts something new.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read this word as the start of the new topic. It belongs to the sentence from the previous דף. The new topic begins with גופא.

phrases.english: [Because of] immorality.
phrases.notes: The end of the previous סוגיא's answer. Some explain it as homosexual behavior, a concern when slaves form a group alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous דף.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Certain groups are not formed for the קרבן פסח because of a concern of immoral behavior.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: three opinions on women and the two פסחs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes in full a ברייתא it cited only partly before. It lists three opinions on whether a woman may have a קרבן פסח slaughtered for her alone, only as part of a group, or not at all, on פסח ראשון and on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the ברייתא itself: A woman on the first פסח: we slaughter for her even by herself. On the second פסח we make her secondary to others (she may only join a group). These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: a woman on the second פסח, we slaughter for her even by herself, and certainly on the first. רבי שמעון says: a woman on the first פסח, we make her secondary to others. On the second פסח, we do not slaughter for her at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to a ברייתא it mentioned briefly earlier, and now quotes it in full. The ברייתא gives three different opinions about women and the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels: (1) slaughter for her alone, (2) she may only join others as a 'side member' (טפילה), (3) not at all. רבי יהודה says level 1 on ראשון and level 2 on שני. רבי יוסי says level 1 on both. רבי שמעון says level 2 on ראשון and level 3 on שני.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': returning to quote and discuss a source cited earlier
The first פסח, on the 14th of ניסן
פסח שני, the make-up פסח a month later on the 14th of אייר
By herself: a קרבן slaughtered with her as the main owner, even with no one else
Secondary to others: she may join a group, but we do not slaughter just for her

steps.whatToRemember: Chart it: רבי יהודה says alone on ראשון, group on שני. רבי יוסי says alone on both. רבי שמעון says group on ראשון, nothing on שני.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Secondary to others' (טפילה) does not mean she is excluded. She may eat from the קרבן as a member of a group. It only means we would not slaughter a קרבן for her by herself.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya explains each of these three positions from the פסוקים. This ברייתא is the base for everything that follows.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: Now the גמרא goes back and quotes in full the source it mentioned earlier.

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה בָּרִאשׁוֹן — שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלֶיהָ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: A woman on the first [פסח]: we slaughter on her behalf by herself,
and on the second we make her secondary to others,
phrases.notes: She may join an existing group, but we do not slaughter for her alone.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: a woman on the second —
we slaughter on her behalf by herself,
and it is unnecessary to say [so] on the first.
Rabbi Shimon says: a woman on the first —
we make her secondary to others,

phrases.aramaic: בַּשֵּׁנִי אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלֶיהָ כָּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: on the second we do not slaughter on her behalf at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new sugya by quoting in full a ברייתא cited earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-way מחלוקת on the status of women for פסח ראשון and פסח שני.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning or פסוקים lead each תנא to his position.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind each of the three opinions. This line sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a request to find the root of the מחלוקת. The answer will show that each תנא reads the relevant פסוקים differently.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they argue?': asking for the underlying basis of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the three opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural or logical basis for each of the three positions.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: women are included on the first פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from 'במכסת נפשות' (by the count of souls) that women are included in the קרבן פסח on פסח ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: 'according to the count of souls' includes even women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with רבי יהודה. He reads the word 'souls' in the פסוק about פסח ראשון as including women, so on ראשון we may slaughter for a woman alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נפשות' (souls) is a word that covers both men and women, unlike 'איש' (man). So on פסח ראשון a woman counts as a full participant. This explains the first half of רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to the count of souls' (שמות יב:ד): the פסוק about counting people for the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
"According to the count of souls",
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ד, said about the first פסח.

phrases.english: and [this includes] even women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving רבי יהודה's source for פסח ראשון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns from 'נפשות' that women are fully included in פסח ראשון.

steps.title: Challenge: then women should be fully included on פסח שני too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a likely objection: if women are included on ראשון, why not equally on שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: if so, then even on the second פסח too [she should be slaughtered for alone]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an objection to its own explanation, before anyone else can. It asks why רבי יהודה doesn't treat women the same way on פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני is normally treated like פסח ראשון. So if women are full participants on ראשון, we would expect them to be full participants on שני as well. That would contradict רבי יהודה's ruling that on שני she is only טפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': the גמרא raising an expected objection itself

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an outside attack that defeats רבי יהודה. The גמרא is anticipating a question while building his view, and it answers right away.

phrases.english: And if you will say,
if so, even on the second also?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ בַּשֵּׁנִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the 'נפשות' reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that on פסח שני a woman is only טפילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'נפשות' includes women on ראשון, and שני follows ראשון, women should be full participants on שני as well.

steps.title: Answer: 'that man shall bear his sin' excludes women on פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about the punishment for skipping פסח שני says 'האיש ההוא' (that man). This shows that only men are obligated in פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'That man shall bear his sin.' A man, yes; a woman, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a פסוק about פסח שני specifically says 'man'. So a woman is not obligated to bring פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (במדבר ט:יג) speaks of someone who missed פסח ראשון and also failed to bring פסח שני. It says 'that man shall bear his sin.' The word 'איש' limits the obligation of שני to men, so we do not slaughter for a woman alone on שני.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That man shall bear his sin' (במדבר ט:יג), said about פסח שני
A man, yes; a woman, no: a limiting דרשה from the word 'איש'

phrases.english: It is written: "That man shall bear his sin."
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:יג, in the passage about פסח שני.

phrases.english: A man, yes; a woman, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with a limiting פסוק specific to פסח שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting פסוק (מיעוט) specific to the second case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שני follows ראשון completely, so women would be included equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק for שני says 'איש', so women are not obligated in פסח שני.

steps.title: Challenge: then women should not even join a group on פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: If women are excluded from פסח שני, why may they even join a group as טפילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: if so, then even as a secondary member she should not [participate] on the second פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second objection in the opposite direction. If 'man' excludes women from פסח שני, why does רבי יהודה let them join a group at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer seemed to remove women from פסח שני entirely. That would fit רבי שמעון's view ('not at all'), not רבי יהודה's view that she may join others. So the גמרא must explain what leftover connection allows her to join.

keyTerms.meaning: Being a secondary member of a group, not the main owner of the קרבן

phrases.english: And if you will say, if so,
even as secondary, she should also not [participate] on the second?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ טְפִילָה נָמֵי בַּשֵּׁנִי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the previous answer to its extreme and challenges רבי יהודה's 'secondary' ruling on שני.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's permission for a woman to join a group as טפילה on פסח שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'איש' excludes women from פסח שני, they should have no part in it at all, not even as group members.

steps.title: Answer: 'like all the laws of the פסח' allows women to join a group
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ככל חקת הפסח' links פסח שני to פסח ראשון. This link is enough to let women join a group on שני as secondary members.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'According to all the statute of the פסח' is effective for [allowing her to be] merely secondary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison of פסח שני to ראשון ('ככל חקת הפסח') still has an effect. It lets a woman be part of a group on שני, even though she is not obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים are balanced. 'איש' removes her obligation, so we do not slaughter for her alone. 'ככל חקת הפסח' links שני back to ראשון, where women are included. So she keeps a partial role: she may join others. This completes רבי יהודה's position.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to all the statute of the פסח' (במדבר ט:יב): compares פסח שני to פסח ראשון

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה uses three פסוקים. 'נפשות' includes women on ראשון. 'האיש ההוא' removes their obligation on שני. 'ככל חקת הפסח' still lets them join a group on שני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: one פסוק limits a law, and another פסוק keeps part of it. The result is a middle-ground ruling.

phrases.english: "According to all the statute of the Paschal offering" is effective
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:יב, comparing the second פסח to the first.

phrases.english: for merely [being] secondary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge, completing the explanation of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second פסוק keeps a partial role (balancing two פסוקים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איש' excludes women from פסח שני entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ככל חקת הפסח' links שני to ראשון enough for women to join a group as טפילה, though we do not slaughter for them alone.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי יוסי and asks for his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving from רבי יהודה's opinion to רבי יוסי's opinion. It is setting up the next move by asking where he gets his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא quoted in step 2, רבי יוסי rules that we may slaughter a פסח for a woman by herself even on פסח שני, which means she is fully obligated. The גמרא now wants the פסוק behind this.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי יהודה's derivation to רבי יוסי's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי יוסי's ruling that women are obligated on פסח שני.

steps.title: The word 'נפש' includes women on both פסחים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns women's obligation on ראשון from 'במכסת נפשות'. He learns it on שני from 'ונכרתה הנפש ההוא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says about the first פסח 'by the count of souls', which includes even a woman. And it says about פסח שני 'that soul shall be cut off from its people'. 'Soul' includes even women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי's source. The word 'soul' (נפש) appears for both פסחים, and a woman is a 'soul' just like a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used 'במכסת נפשות' only for ראשון. רבי יוסי adds the כרת verse for שני, which also uses the word נפש. Since women can be liable for כרת on שני, they must be obligated in פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Soul / person; a word that includes both men and women
Shall be cut off (the punishment of כָּרֵת)

phrases.english: As it is written regarding the first: 'by the count of souls' — even a woman,
and it is written regarding the second Pesach:
'that soul shall be cut off from its people,'
'soul' — even women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word נפש, used for ראשון ('במכסת נפשות') and for the כרת of שני ('ונכרתה הנפש'), includes women.

steps.title: Then what does 'that man' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The same verse also says 'האיש ההוא'. This seems to limit the obligation to men, so what does it exclude according to רבי יוסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then 'that man shall bear his sin' — what does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי with the end of the very same פסוק. That part says 'man', which רבי יהודה used to exclude women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'נפש' includes women, the word 'איש' seems to have no purpose. The Torah does not waste words, so רבי יוסי must explain what 'איש' excludes.

phrases.english: But then: 'that man shall bear his sin' —
to exclude what?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא חֶטְאוֹ יִשָּׂא הָאִישׁ הַהוּא לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's reading of the verse used in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that women are included on פסח שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'איש' in the same verse seems to exclude women, so it must exclude something.

steps.title: 'Man' excludes a minor from כרת
steps.stepSummary: 'איש' comes to exclude a קטן from the punishment of כרת, not to exclude women.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude a minor from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי. 'Man' here means an adult, so the word excludes a child, not a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איש' can mean 'male' or 'adult'. רבי יהודה read it as male, which excludes women. רבי יוסי reads it as adult, which excludes a minor from כרת. That way both words in the verse have a job.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי ignores the word 'איש'. He uses it, but reads it as excluding a child rather than a woman.

phrases.english: To exclude a minor from karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word 'איש' as adult rather than male.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'איש' excludes a קטן from כרת, and women remain included through 'נפש'.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: 'נפש' includes women on both פסחים, and 'האיש ההוא' only excludes a קטן from כרת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: 'man' on ראשון excludes women
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from the word 'איש' on פסח ראשון that a man, not a woman, is the main subject of the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון: it is written about the first 'man'. A man, yes; a woman, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי שמעון's view. He holds that even on ראשון a woman cannot have a פסח brought for her on her own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון disagrees with both רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about ראשון. He finds the word 'איש' in a פסח ראשון verse and reads it as excluding women. Which verse this is will be asked in step 20.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon: it is written regarding the first 'man,'
a man — yes; a woman — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 9–10, now giving רבי שמעון's source (the question 'what is his reason' is implied).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'איש' on ראשון excludes women from being main members of the פסח.

steps.title: Then women should not even join as טפילה
steps.stepSummary: If 'איש' excludes women, they should not even be able to join a group as secondary members.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if so, then even as טפילה they should not join?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון. If women are excluded, why does he allow them to join a group on ראשון at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון rules that on ראשון women join as טפילה. But an exclusion from 'איש' sounds complete, so it should block even that.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces an expected objection)
Secondary / attached member of a group

phrases.english: And if you say: if so,
even as secondary, also not?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ טְפִילָה נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of the exclusion from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's allowance of women as טפילה on ראשון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A total exclusion from 'איש' should remove women from the פסח entirely.

steps.title: 'במכסת נפשות' allows women as טפילה
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'במכסת נפשות' works to include women as secondary members.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'By the count of souls' is effective for him to include women as secondary members.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a second verse balances the first. 'איש' blocks women as main members, and 'נפשות' brings them back as secondary members.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון uses the same verse רבי יהודה used, but gives it a smaller job. For him it only lets women join as טפילה, not as fully obligated members.

phrases.english: 'By the count of souls' is effective for him for secondary status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Balancing two verses: one excludes, the other partially includes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women are fully excluded on ראשון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are excluded as main members but included as טפילה through 'במכסת נפשות'.

steps.title: Then women should join as טפילה on שני too
steps.stepSummary: If women join as טפילה on ראשון, they should be able to do the same on שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: even on the second as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Since שני follows the rules of ראשון, women should be טפילה on שני too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון rules that on שני women cannot join at all. The challenge asks what makes שני different from ראשון.

phrases.english: And if you say: even on the second as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the conclusion of step 15 to שני and asks why it does not apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that women do not join at all on שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'במכסת נפשות' allows טפילה on ראשון, the same should apply on שני.

steps.title: The Torah excluded women on שני with 'האיש'
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'חטאו ישא האיש' on שני excludes women.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah excluded on the second, as it is written 'that man shall bear his sin'. A man, yes; a woman, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a separate word on פסח שני removes women from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same word רבי יהודה used and רבי יוסי applied to a קטן. רבי שמעון reads it as excluding women from שני. The next step clarifies exactly what it excludes them from.

phrases.english: The Merciful One excluded on the second,
as it is written: 'that man shall bear his sin,'
a man — yes; a woman — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate exclusion verse specific to שני.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women join as טפילה on שני just like on ראשון.

steps.title: From what exactly does the verse exclude women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the exclusion is from obligation or from joining as טפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what does it exclude her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to pin down the exact effect of 'האיש' on שני. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possibilities. The verse could exclude women from being obligated, or from joining as secondary members. Only the second would support רבי שמעון's ruling.

phrases.english: From what does it exclude her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the scope of the exclusion in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'האיש' on שני excludes women from obligation or from טפילה.

steps.title: It must exclude women even from טפילה
steps.stepSummary: Women are not obligated even on ראשון, so it would be obvious they are not obligated on שני. The verse must therefore exclude them from טפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If from obligation — now, on the first she is not obligated; is it needed for the second? Rather, is it not from being secondary?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its point by elimination. Excluding women from obligation on שני would teach nothing new, so the verse must exclude them from joining as secondary members.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, women are not obligated even on ראשון. שני is only a make-up for ראשון, so of course they are not obligated on it. A verse is never wasted on the obvious, so the exclusion must be from טפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens a 'now that' kind of logic)
Is it necessary (to say)? This is obvious

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains רבי שמעון's whole position in the ברייתא: on ראשון women join only as טפילה, and on שני not at all.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: 'איש' on ראשון excludes women as main members, 'במכסת נפשות' lets them be טפילה, and 'האיש' on שני removes even that.

phrases.english: If from obligation —
now, on the first she is not obligated,
is it necessary to say on the second?
Rather, is it not from secondary status?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מֵחִיּוּב הַשְׁתָּא בָּרִאשׁוֹן לָא בַּשֵּׁנִי מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by eliminating the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse excludes women from joining as טפילה on שני, since excluding them from obligation would be obvious.

steps.title: Which 'איש' verse did רבי שמעון mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק about פסח ראשון contains the word 'איש' that רבי שמעון relies on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the 'man' that רבי שמעון spoke of?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to step 13 to identify the exact verse. It is setting up an examination of possible candidates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several פסח verses say 'איש', and some are already used for other teachings. The גמרא must find one that is free for רבי שמעון's exclusion of women.

phrases.english: And what is the 'man' that Rabbi Shimon spoke of?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the unspecified verse cited in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific פסח ראשון verse with 'איש' that רבי שמעון uses.

steps.title: Not 'ויקחו להם איש שה' — that verse teaches רבי יצחק's rule
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion, 'ויקחו להם איש שה', is rejected. That verse is needed for רבי יצחק's teaching that an adult can acquire for others but a minor cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say 'They shall take for themselves every man a lamb for a father's house…', that verse is needed for רבי יצחק, who said: a man acquires, but a minor does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a verse and immediately rejects it. That 'איש' is already used for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ויקחו להם איש שה' is the obvious candidate. But רבי יצחק learns from its 'איש' that only an adult can acquire a portion of the קרבן on behalf of others, and a minor cannot. Since that word is already used, it is not available for רבי שמעון, and the search continues.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'איש' versus 'קטן' is about age (adult vs. minor), not male vs. female. The verse is rejected because its word 'איש' is already used for רבי יצחק's teaching, so it is not free for רבי שמעון's exclusion of women.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נֵימָא: ״וְיִקְחוּ לָהֶם אִישׁ שֶׂה לְבֵית אָבוֹת וְגוֹ׳״ —
phrases.english: If we say: 'They shall take for themselves every man a lamb for a father's house, etc.' —
that one he needs for the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak,
who said: a man acquires,
but a minor does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא וְיִקְחוּ לָהֶם אִישׁ שֶׂה לְבֵית אָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'ויקחו להם איש שה' as רבי שמעון's source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'איש' in that verse is already used for רבי יצחק's rule that only an adult can acquire on behalf of others.

steps.title: A second suggested verse for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Having rejected 'ויקחו להם איש שה', the גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון's 'איש' comes from 'מאיש לפי אכלו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps it comes from 'according to every man's eating'.
steps.whatsHappening: The first verse was rejected, so the גמרא now tries a different verse about פסח ראשון that contains the word 'איש'. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון needs a verse about the first פסח that says 'איש', a man, so he can exclude women. 'מאיש לפי אכלו' (שמות יב:ד) is about the first פסח and contains that word, so it is a natural next candidate.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new attempt after the last one failed)
According to each man's eating (שמות יב:ד)

phrases.english: Rather, from "according to every man's eating"
phrases.notes: A new suggested source for רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement verse after step 21 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source may be 'מאיש לפי אכלו'.

steps.title: That verse is needed for slaughtering for one person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי agrees with רבי שמעון on one point, so רבי שמעון presumably agrees with רבי יוסי as well. In that case he needs 'מאיש לפי אכלו' to teach that a פסח may be slaughtered for a single person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since רבי יוסי holds like רבי שמעון, רבי שמעון also holds like רבי יוסי. And he needs that verse to teach that we may slaughter the פסח for an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new suggestion. It says this verse is already being used for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תנאים are assumed to share the same overall approach. If so, רבי שמעון accepts רבי יוסי's rule that a פסח may be offered for a single person, and that rule comes from this verse. A verse that is already used for one law cannot simply be borrowed for another.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the verse is already used for something else)

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: But since Rabbi Yosei holds like Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: Refers to an earlier agreement between them (about offering the פסח on a במה).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon also holds like Rabbi Yosei,
and he needs that verse
to teach that we slaughter the Paschal lamb for an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the verse suggested in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'מאיש לפי אכלו' as רבי שמעון's source for excluding women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is already needed for the rule that a פסח may be slaughtered for one person, which רבי שמעון accepts.

steps.title: The extra word 'איש' teaches a second law
steps.stepSummary: To teach about slaughtering for one person, the תורה could have written just 'לפי אכלו'. The extra word 'איש' teaches the second law: only men are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would answer you: if so, the Torah should have written only 'according to his eating'. Why does it add 'man'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the suggestion. The verse can teach two laws at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לפי אכלו' (his eating, in the singular) are enough to teach that one person may bring a פסח. The added word 'איש' is therefore extra, and it teaches that the obligation is on men and not women. So the verse teaches both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns two laws from 'מאיש לפי אכלו': a פסח may be slaughtered for one person ('לפי אכלו'), and the extra word 'איש' excludes women from פסח ראשון.

phrases.english: He would say to you: If so,
let the Torah write "according to his eating."
phrases.notes: That alone would teach the rule about an individual.

phrases.english: Why "man"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִם כֵּן נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word (ייתור) allows a double teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is used up by the rule about a single person.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לפי אכלו' teaches the single-person rule, and the extra 'איש' excludes women.

steps.title: Whose view is רבי אלעזר's rule about women?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר said: for a woman, the first פסח is mandatory, the second is optional, and it overrides שבת. The גמרא asks which תנא this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view matches what רבי אלעזר said: a woman is obligated on the first, the second is optional, and it overrides שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי אלעזר and asks which תנא it matches. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several תנאים gave different views on women and the two פסחים. The גמרא wants to match רבי אלעזר to one of them. Before it can do that, the wording will turn out to be problematic.

keyTerms.meaning: Overrides שבת (may be done even on שבת)

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which Rabbi Elazar said:
A woman on the first Pesach is obligatory,
and on the second it is optional, and it overrides Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the three opinions of the ברייתא (step 2) to match an אמורא's ruling to one of them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view רבי אלעזר follows.

steps.title: Something optional cannot override שבת
steps.stepSummary: If the second פסח is only optional for her, how can it override שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is optional, why does it override שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא points out a problem in רבי אלעזר's wording itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a required offering can push aside the strict laws of שבת. An optional act cannot do that. So the statement, as worded, contradicts itself.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רְשׁוּת, אַמַּאי דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת?
phrases.english: If it is optional, why does it override Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רְשׁוּת, אַמַּאי דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the statement quoted in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ובשני רשות ודוחה את השבת'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only an obligation can override שבת; something optional cannot.

steps.title: Reorder the statement
steps.stepSummary: Reread it: the second is optional, the first is mandatory, and the first overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: on the second it is optional, and on the first it is mandatory and overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording so that 'overrides שבת' is attached to the mandatory first פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself stays the same: the first is mandatory and the second is optional. Only the order changes, so that overriding שבת belongs to the first פסח, where the woman is obligated.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing the law about which פסח is mandatory. It is only moving 'overrides שבת' so that it applies to the first, obligatory פסח.

phrases.english: Rather, say: on the second it is optional,
and on the first it is obligatory and overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of step 26 by reordering the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The optional second פסח overrides שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mandatory first פסח is what overrides שבת.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Once the wording is fixed, רבי אלעזר's statement matches רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question from step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה held that a woman is obligated on the first פסח and optional on the second. That is exactly the corrected statement of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר follows רבי יהודה: for a woman, the first פסח is mandatory and overrides שבת, and the second is optional.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25's question using the corrected text from step 27.

steps.title: Do not form a פסח group made up only of converts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a חבורה should not consist entirely of גרים, because they might be overly exacting and end up disqualifying the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: we do not form a group made up entirely of converts, because they may be too exacting with it and cause it to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, separate teaching about who should make up a פסח group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גרים may be very eager but less familiar with the details of the laws. They might add needless strictness and treat a valid קרבן as invalid. Mixing them with experienced Jews prevents this.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered together on one פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the חכמים set up the group's makeup to protect the קרבן from being wrongly disqualified.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
We do not make a group that is entirely converts,
lest they be overly exacting with it
and bring it to disqualification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New independent teaching about forming a פסח group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח group may not be made up entirely of גרים, lest they be overly exacting and disqualify the offering.

steps.title: A ברייתא on eating פסח, מצה and מרור
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that eating פסח, מצה and מרור is a must on the first night and optional afterward. רבי שמעון says it is a must for men and optional for women.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: פסח, מצה and מרור are a must on the first night, and from then on they are optional. רבי שמעון says: for men it is a must, and for women it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists three פסח foods. It says when eating them is required and when it is optional, and it adds a view from רבי שמעון about women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different splits appear here. The first split is about time: the first night versus the rest of the days. The second split is about people: men versus women, in רבי שמעון's view. The ברייתא does not clearly say which food each split applies to, and that gap is what the גמרא will examine next.

keyTerms.meaning: From here on, meaning the remaining days of פסח.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The Paschal lamb, matza and bitter herbs,
on the first night are mandatory,
from here on are optional.
phrases.notes: 'From here on' means the rest of פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
For men it is mandatory, and for women it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a new ברייתא about obligations, which connects to the earlier discussion of women and the קרבן פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating פסח, מצה and מרור is a must on the first night and optional afterward. According to רבי שמעון, it is a must for men and optional for women.

steps.title: Which food does the 'optional' line refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא the phrase 'from then on, optional' is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this referring to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: which foods does the 'optional afterward' line mean? This question sets up the next steps, where the גמרא tests each possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three foods together, but the 'optional afterward' rule may not fit all three. The גמרא wants to know exactly which food the rule covers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On which one does it stand?', meaning 'what does this refer to?'

phrases.english: To which part does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This questions the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which food the clause 'from then on, optional' applies to.

steps.title: It cannot refer to the פסח, because there is no פסח all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The first option is that the line refers to the קרבן פסח. That fails, because the קרבן פסח is only eaten on the first night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the פסח: is there a פסח all seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that 'optional afterward' is about the קרבן פסח, and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח is eaten only on the first night. On the later days there is no קרבן פסח at all. So it makes no sense to call eating it 'optional' on those days.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say', which introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to test.
'Is there?', a question that expects the answer 'no'.

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the Paschal lamb,
is there a Paschal lamb all seven days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'from then on, optional' refers to the קרבן פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרבן פסח only exists on the first night, so it cannot be 'optional' on the days after.

steps.title: If it refers to מצה and מרור, the end of the ברייתא is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The second option is that the line is about מצה and מרור. But then רבי שמעון's 'optional for women' would also be about מצה, and that is hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it refers to מצה and מרור, look at the end of the ברייתא: רבי שמעון says it is a must for men and optional for women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second possibility and points to the last line of the ברייתא. This step sets up the real challenge, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole ברייתא is about מצה and מרור, then רבי שמעון would be saying that women do not have to eat מצה. The גמרא now prepares to show that this cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But rather', which introduces the next option after the first one failed.
'Say the end clause', meaning 'look at what the end of the source says'.

phrases.english: Rather, if it refers to matza and bitter herbs,
then say the latter clause:
Rabbi Shimon says:
For men it is mandatory and for women it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This moves to the second possible answer after step 32 rejected the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that applies the whole ברייתא, including רבי שמעון's line, to מצה and מרור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, רבי שמעון would be exempting women from מצה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר proves that women are obligated in מצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי אלעזר. He learns from a פסוק that anyone forbidden to eat חמץ must also eat מצה, and women are forbidden to eat חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון not accept what רבי אלעזר said? רבי אלעזר said that women are obligated to eat מצה by Torah law, because the פסוק says: 'Do not eat חמץ with it; for seven days eat מצות with it.' Whoever is under the ban on eating חמץ is also under the command to eat מצה. Women are under the ban on חמץ, so they are also under the command to eat מצה!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual challenge. The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's proof that women must eat מצה, so רבי שמעון cannot be saying that מצה is optional for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the ban on חמץ and the command to eat מצה side by side, which ties them together. Women keep all the 'do not' commands of the Torah, including the ban on חמץ. Because of the link, they are also included in the command to eat מצה. So 'optional for women' cannot be about מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Doesn't he hold?', a challenge asking whether a תנא really rejects an accepted rule.
By Torah law, not only a rabbinic rule.
'Get up and eat מצה', the positive command to eat מצה.

steps.confusionAlert: Women are usually exempt from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, a positive command tied to a set time. Eating מצה is such a command, yet women are obligated in it. That is only because of the special link in the פסוק to the ban on חמץ. Do not think that the general exemption applies here.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that women are fully obligated to eat מצה at the סדר by Torah law.

phrases.english: Does Rabbi Shimon not accept
that which Rabbi Elazar said:
Women are obligated in eating matza
by Torah law,
as it is stated: 'You shall not eat leavened bread with it;'
'seven days you shall eat matzot with it'.
Whoever is subject to the ban on eating leavened bread
is subject to the command to arise and eat matza.
And these women,
since they are subject to the ban on eating leavened bread,
they are subject to the command to arise and eat matza!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes the challenge that step 33 began, using רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: A reading of רבי שמעון in which מצה is optional for women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר derives from the פסוק that women are obligated in מצה, because the command to eat מצה is linked to the ban on חמץ.

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא: רבי שמעון's line is only about the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread. 'Optional afterward' refers to מצה and מרור, and רבי שמעון's men-versus-women split refers only to the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: פסח, מצה and מרור are a must on the first night, and from then on they are optional. רבי שמעון says: the פסח is a must for men and optional for women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא so that both problems go away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Optional afterward' now refers only to מצה and מרור. That works, because those foods exist all week while the קרבן פסח does not. רבי שמעון's split between men and women is now only about the קרבן פסח. That fits his view, seen earlier, that women's participation in the פסח is optional. Women stay obligated in מצה, just as רבי אלעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say': this introduces a corrected reading of a source.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three results. First, after the first night, eating מצה and מרור is optional. Second, according to רבי שמעון, women's participation in the קרבן פסח is optional. Third, women are obligated in מצה by Torah law, based on רבי אלעזר's rule.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
The Paschal lamb, matza and bitter herbs
on the first night are mandatory;
from here on, eating matza and bitter herbs is optional.
Rabbi Shimon says:
The Paschal lamb is mandatory for men
and optional for women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This resolves the challenges in steps 32 to 34 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected reading: each clause of the ברייתא is matched to a different food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every clause of the ברייתא applies to all three foods.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Optional afterward' applies to מצה and מרור, and רבי שמעון's men-versus-women split applies only to the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: A mourner may eat his Paschal lamb at night, but not other sacrificial food
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an אונן immerses and eats his קרבן פסח in the evening, but may not eat other קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A mourner on the day of a close relative's death immerses and eats his Paschal lamb that night, but he may not eat other sacrificial foods.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a ruling about an אונן. He is allowed to eat the קרבן פסח at night, but not other קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן is forbidden to eat קדשים. מן התורה this applies only during the day of the death, and the רבנן extended it to include the night as well. For the קרבן פסח, which carries a כרת obligation, the רבנן did not apply their extension, so he eats it at night. For all other קדשים their extension stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A mourner on the day of a close relative's death, before burial. He is forbidden to eat קדשים.
In the evening, meaning the night after the day of death.
Sacrificial foods in general, other than the פסח.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אונן may eat all קדשים at night. The משנה makes an exception only for the קרבן פסח. Other קדשים stay forbidden at night because of the רבנן's extension.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the רבנן sometimes hold back their own decree when it would block a Torah obligation as serious as the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Heading that marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: An acute mourner immerses and eats
phrases.notes: אונן means a mourner on the day of the death.

phrases.english: his Paschal lamb in the evening,
but not other sacrificial foods.
phrases.notes: For these, the רבנן's rule that אנינות carries on into the night still holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אוֹנֵן — טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לָעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is unrelated to the previous discussion about מצה, מרור, and women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן immerses and eats his קרבן פסח at night, but may not eat other קדשים.

steps.title: Opening a new case: one who hears about a relative's death
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a second case, about someone who hears of a relative's death only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who hears about the death of his relative...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up a new case, a person who only learns later that a close relative died. Its ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different situation from the אונן above. Here the person was not present on the day of death and finds out afterward. Whether he still has the status of אנינות, and how it affects eating קדשים, will be explained in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hears, meaning he receives the news.
His dead, meaning a close relative who died.

phrases.english: One who hears about his dead relative,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup line (part of the same משנה)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the same משנה. It contrasts with the regular אונן of step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of someone who hears of a relative's death later. The ruling follows on the next amud.
